Figure 2 presents a comparison of inference times for baseline Llama models and their distilled MambalLlama counterparts at two different scales: 1B and 3B parameters. In subplot (a), labeled "1B Models," the x-axis represents batch size on a linear scale ranging from 1 to 300, with tick marks at intervals of 15 (1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 300). The y-axis shows inference time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 10, with tick marks every 2 seconds. Three bars are shown for each batch size: blue for Llama-1B, orange for Llama-1B (hybrid), and red for MambalLlama-1B. The inference time increases with batch size for all models. At a batch size of 1, the inference times are approximately 2.6, 2.6, and 2.6 seconds for Llama-1B, Llama-1B (hybrid), and MambalLlama-1B, respectively. At batch size 300, the times are approximately 8.7, 8.7, and 8.7 seconds. The speedup values (shown as text above the red bars) indicate that MambalLlama-1B is faster than the baseline Llama-1B, with speedups ranging from ×1.6 at batch size 1 to ×3.7 at batch size 300.

In subplot (b), labeled "3B Models," the x-axis again represents batch size on a linear scale, ranging from 1 to 512, with tick marks at intervals of 15 (1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512). The y-axis shows inference time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks every 5 seconds. The same three models are compared: blue for Llama-3B, orange for Llama-3B (hybrid), and red for MambalLlama-3B. Inference time increases with batch size. At batch size 1, the inference times are approximately 2.6, 2.6, and 2.6 seconds for Llama-3B, Llama-3B (hybrid), and MambalLlama-3B, respectively. At batch size 512, the times are approximately 24.2, 24.2, and 0.9 seconds. The speedup values indicate that MambalLlama-3B is significantly faster, with a speedup of ×26.8 at batch size 512. The figure demonstrates that the MambalLlama models generate tokens much faster than the baseline Llama models, with the performance advantage increasing with batch size, especially at the 3B scale.
